create.name: Deng Ming-Dao
create.bio:
Deng Ming-Dao is an American writer, artist and book designer whose books bring Taoist philosophy into ordinary daily life. He grew up in a San Francisco studio as the son of the potter and author Jade Snow Wong, and in 1975 took up the formal study of Taoism, qigong and the Chinese martial arts. His longest-standing teacher was Kwan Saihung, whose life he retold in a trilogy later gathered into one volume as Chronicles of Tao; he also trained with Zhang Hongmei and other masters, learned yoga from Baba Hari Dass, and received Dzogchen teachings in the lineage of the Dalai Lama.

His best-loved book is 365 Tao, a year of short daily reflections, and later titles include Everyday Tao, Scholar Warrior, The Living I Ching, The Lunar Tao and The Pattern of Change. A new translation with commentary, The Complete Dàodéjīng, is due in January 2027, with free online talks around its launch. Between 2013 and 2023 he taught courses in qigong, Taijiquan, Xingyiquan, Baguazhang and Taoist philosophy; these days he shares the practice mainly through his books, a blog series on following the Dao, and long podcast conversations about qi, the I Ching and living in step with the Tao. He also paints in ink and watercolour.

books.title: Chronicles of Tao: The Secret Life of a Taoist Master
books.author: Deng Ming-Dao
books.description: A single revised volume of his first three books, a novelised life of his teacher Kwan Saihung from boyhood training on a sacred mountain to later life.

books.title: The Lunar Tao: Meditations in Harmony with the Seasons
books.author: Deng Ming-Dao
books.description: A daily reader that follows the Chinese lunar calendar, pairing each day with a short meditation and notes on the festivals and stories tied to Taoist tradition.

books.title: The Pattern of Change: A Mathematical and Philosophical Study of How We See the World
books.author: Deng Ming-Dao
books.description: Written with the mathematician Robert V. Moody, a long study of pattern and change that sets ideas from mathematics and physics beside Chinese philosophical thought.

free_resources.title: The Complete Dàodéjīng publication events
free_resources.description: Three free Zoom events in January 2027 for his new translation of the Dàodéjīng: a seminar on ten key ideas in the text, a publication-day gathering and a question-and-answer session, with recordings shared afterwards.

free_resources.title: Blog series on following the Dao
free_resources.description: Free essay series on his site, including core ideas for following the Dao and a fifteen-part series on why he practises martial arts and spirituality.
